$comment: WHAT `eas submit` UPLOADS A BUILD TO. Nothing here can be filled in before
the store records exist: App Store Connect assigns ascAppId when the app is
created, and appleTeamId comes off the developer portal's Membership page.
`make store-preflight` names both while they are missing.
THE THREE ascApiKey* FIELDS ARE `$VAR` REFERENCES, AND THAT IS THE POINT.
EAS interpolates the process environment into exactly those three iOS submit
fields, so the credential stays out of a public tree while a
--non-interactive submit still works. It reads the PROCESS environment and
not native/.env, so export them (or set them as CI secrets) first — fastlane
loads the file on its own, `eas submit` does not.
The other two ids are committed literals because EAS does NOT interpolate
them and there is no CLI flag for either. Both are public: an Apple app id
is in the App Store URL and a team id is on every app the team ships.
